perspective:
From Alice Lim’s perspective, she has access to the following:

- She is Alice Lim, a dental hygienist. She knows her own healthcare experience, feelings, intentions, and actions.
- Austin Moreno is her old friend from high school. They have stayed close, discuss personal and professional lives, and support each other. Through their friendship, she knows he works in insurance, though the dialogue itself only shows her asking generally about “work” and “the office.”
- At coffee, she observed Austin acting reserved when work came up. She asked if things were okay. Austin said it was “nothing really,” just usual ups and downs, then said he wasn’t sure how to handle a few complicated things at work. She told him he could talk to her. She suspected something specific was bothering him and that he might be hiding something about his job performance.
- She later worried Austin might be considering a career change. She asked if he had thought about changing careers. Austin said he had thought about it but didn’t know what other paths to take and asked for suggestions. She suggested healthcare, offered to tell him about her experiences, and offered to connect him with contacts. Austin said it sounded interesting and wanted to know more.
- She sensed Austin was hesitant because of fear of the unknown. She told him about her friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and was happier. Austin said that was inspiring but worried about risks and initial struggle. Alice encouraged him about growth through leaving comfort zones and said she would support him. Austin thanked her, saying her support and real success stories helped.
- She offered to connect Austin with a career counselor and friends in healthcare. Austin appreciated it. She planned to set up a meeting next week.
- After several discussions and meetings, she believed Austin was ready to take next steps and appreciated her help. She felt satisfaction and joy. She told Austin she was proud of his steps. Austin said he felt excited, nervous, and grateful. She proposed regular check-ins; Austin agreed, saying they would keep him focused and that her perspective was helpful.

She does not have access to hidden details about Austin’s actual job performance, private motives, or narrator-only traits unless he told her or she observed them.
